text:
Maria G.: Starting a staging canary for inference-service v2 -> 5% traffic, 15m window. Posting here for rollback notes and watchers.
Jon P.: ack. I’m watching latency and 5xxs.
Lee W.: FYI console shows small spike in 5xxs around minute 6, sampling traces. TraceId: 0x9f3b.
Sam H.: Can we hold on auto-promotion? I want to validate cache behavior first (session affinity + KV).
Maria G.: auto-promo is off. This is manual canary only.
Eva (deploy-bot): deploy started: canary id=canary-2026-03-18-01, tier=staging, split=5% -> backends: v1(95%), v2(5%).
Aisha: quick note — if we revert, session stickiness could still route a subset to v2 for a bit. We should evict session keys for the canary prefix.
Jon P.: Good catch. What's the exact prefix?
Aisha: sessions keyed as `session:{route}:{model_version}`; canary used `model_version=v2-canary`. So evict `session:*:v2-canary`.
Lee W.: Suggestion for rollback sequence (minimal downtime):
- pause new canary traffic (set split=0)
- mark canary hosts draining=true so they finish in-flight requests
- evict session prefix for v2-canary from KV/cache
- verify no requests hitting v2 for 2x P95 window
- decommission canary pods
Sam H.: + ensure we don't do a full global cache flush. Targeted eviction only. Full flush will wreck production latency.
Maria G.: If we need to execute quickly, who triggers the override? I can do it but want a quick comms plan.
Jon P.: I can run the override and the targeted eviction. Two-step safe revert command sequence I use:
```bash
# step 1: cut traffic to 0
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  "https://console.internal/api/rollouts/canary-override" \
  -d '{"canary_id":"canary-2026-03-18-01","override_split":0}'
# step 2: evict canary session keys
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  "https://console.internal/api/cache/evict" -d '{"prefix":"session:*:v2-canary"}'
```
Aisha: After we cut traffic, also change routing policy fast-fail to fallback model to avoid any stray routing heuristics hitting v2.
Lee W.: Telemetry checklist after override: check per-route 5xx, per-host CPU, kv-hit-rate for session prefix, and traces for any rerouted requests. I’ll keep a 1h watch.
Sam H.: One extra gotcha — dedicated endpoints with pinned model_version might still accept requests. We should update route-level guards: `allowed_model_versions` to remove `v2-canary` if present.
Maria G.: Understood. I’ll post status updates in this thread as I act. Starting override now.
Maria G.: (10s) Override API call done. Response: 200.
Eva (deploy-bot): override applied: canary-2026-03-18-01 split=0 -> effective routing: v1 100%
Jon P.: Eviction job queued.
Jon P.: Eviction job running...
Jon P.: Eviction job completed (removed ~18k keys, duration 7s).
Lee W.: KV hit-rate for `session:*:v2-canary` is now 0, traces show no new v2 hits for last 3 mins.
Sam H.: Marking canary hosts draining=true via admin API.
Aisha: I updated route guard to drop `v2-canary` from allowed_model_versions.
Maria G.: Good. Any telem alarms to silence? We’ll keep the alerting but add a note to incident to avoid paging for expected flaps.
Lee W.: I’ll mute the noisy alert for next 30m.
Maria G.: Decommissioning canary pods now.
Eva (deploy-bot): canary pods terminated: 3 instances removed.
Jon P.: Final sanity: run smoke test against a few customer-like payloads -> all responses from v1 and latency within baseline.
Sam H.: Smoke tests passed.
Maria G.: Thanks all. Follow-up TODOs: add a one-click "fast-exit + targeted-evict" button in Console for rollouts, and document session-key patterns in the runbook. Filing a ticket: PRODENG-4123.
Aisha: Also add an operator hint in Console that warns about pinned endpoints during rollback.
Lee W.: Good call. I’ll add telemetry dashboard panels for canary session keys next week.
Maria G.: Closing thread — we’ll re-run canary after the runbook updates. :thumbsup:
